# Xbox Exit / System menu

On Xbox, selecting **Exit / System...** or pressing B/Escape at the title opens:

- Cancel
- Return to launcher
- Restart game
- Reboot Xbox
- Power off Xbox

Cancel is selected initially in both the menu and every confirmation. B/Escape
backs out of a confirmation to the menu, then back to the title. Selecting an
action never executes it immediately: choose its confirmation explicitly.
Desktop exit behavior is unchanged. The in-level Give Up action still abandons
the level; it is not a console power action.

All confirmed actions go through Neverball's normal settings, game, audio,
joystick and SDL cleanup before the platform dispatches them. An append-only
`D:\system-actions.log` records the selected action and completed cleanup.
The shutdown watchdog has a 15-second recovery timeout; recovery from a wedged
kernel/GPU is not guaranteed.

## Launcher and restart targets

Return to launcher opens `E:\Dashboard\default.xbe` by default, matching this
rig's Slime Volley setup. It is a private-rig default, not a universal dashboard
location. This executable was read back and matched against XBMC's running
`/Q/default.xbe` (SHA-256
`2cbfeeb3e888e8df74316b33ea0ab056c2ea401ad09032507fed06a59fd9bbbe`).

Other installations can place one native absolute XBE path on the first line
of `Neverball/xbox-launcher.txt` beside the game's data, for example:

```text
E:\Apps\XBMC\default.xbe
```

The target is checked before confirmation and again before teardown. Missing
or invalid targets show an error and keep Neverball running. To restore the
default, remove that override file from the Xbox installation. The deployment
helper preserves user files and does not automatically delete this override.

Restart game uses NXDK's full native path to the running XBE rather than a
relative `D:\default.xbe`. Native-path preflight uses a rootless NT file open,
following NXDK's `hal/xbox.c`; DOS-drive paths use file attributes. Reboot Xbox
uses the normal firmware reboot path. Power off uses the Xbox SMC shutdown
request, as in the reference port. A failed launch or power request falls back
to a firmware reboot after logging.

## Source and validation

The menu/action pattern is adapted from the hardware-tested
[Slime Volley Xbox port](https://github.com/ZacharyLeahan/slimevolley-nxdk),
specifically [Platform.c at 65c86911](https://github.com/ZacharyLeahan/slimevolley-nxdk/blob/65c86911fe5ab199e7853886af7c71d8ad1e5085/ports/nxdk/Platform.c).
The implementation uses Neverball's existing GUI/state system. It retains the
original Neverball and JayFoxRox/Jannik Vogel port notices and dependency
attribution.

Host verification: full NXDK XBE build, desktop unit tests, and
`python3 tests/check-xbox-exit.py`. The latter exercises the real action
handler under address/undefined-behavior sanitizers with mocked system actions:
all four confirmation/cancel paths, missing targets, target disappearance
between selection and confirmation, and invalid menu values.

Launcher return, game restart and firmware reboot passed on hardware with
normal audio/SDL cleanup recorded. Cancel/default selection and the
unavailable-target screen were also exercised.

Physical tests use only the 128 MiB original Xbox and the separate
`/F/neverball-upstream` installation. No emulator or known-good installation
change is involved. Exact results and candidate hashes are recorded in
[the hardware ledger](hardware-testing.md). Actual power-off is not exercised
in this run so the console and KVM remain available; its confirmation/cancel
flow is tested, and its SMC dispatch is inherited from the tested reference.
